result.title: Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithms
result.summary: Adversarial sharpness penalty per iteration of a base optimizer, known as sharpness-aware minimization (SAM), is an accepted technique to improve generalization in deep learning. Recently, Muon has emerged as a dominant optimization algorithm for training large language models (LLMs). It achieves lower sample complexity for heavy-tailed gradient updates - a phenomenon common in LLM training. However, sharpness penalties with Muon updates are yet largely unexplored in the literature. Moreover, the behavior of SAM under heavy-tailed noise is unknown both theoretically and empirically. A potential reason for this gap is the additional cost of extra gradient computation per iteration for penalty perturbations in SAM, which becomes prohibitive for LLMs. This paper introduces Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithm (SOMA) to combine a computationally efficient and theoretically grounded perturbation scheme with the Muon algorithm. The key idea is to use stale (purely) stochastic gradient noise for adversarial perturbations. Theoretically, we show that SOMA's sample complexity is invariant to the perturbation direction. We provide explorations and insights into SOMA's robustness to heavy-tailed gradient noise. We extensively explore SOMA's efficacy in (a) mitigating quality degradation due to post-training quantization, and (b) catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning of LLMs.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 SOMA，将一种计算更省、理论上有依据的扰动方案（利用过时的纯随机梯度噪声）与 Muon 优化器结合，用于减轻后训练量化带来的质量下降和微调中的灾难性遗忘。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是面向 LLM 训练的优化算法与泛化/鲁棒性研究，未涉及视觉推理状态、证据获取、停止决策或 latent 表示，仅“微调稳定性”与轨迹训练有极弱关联，缺少可核查的具体借鉴线索。
